requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data (LVM PV/VG/LV chain, filesystem, mount)
requirements.summary: pvcreate/vgcreate vgdata/lvcreate lvdata created on a loop-backed PV (no spare disk existed), formatted xfs, mounted at /srv/data with `df -h` confirming the mount; data was seeded and initial sha256 checksums verified OK.

requirements.requirement: Grow the LV to at least 2 GB while it stays mounted and contents stay intact
requirements.summary: Single evidenced command block shows pre-growth checksum OK and mount present, a second loop-backed PV added via vgextend, `lvextend -L +1300M` and online `xfs_growfs` performed without unmounting, resulting LV size <2.25 GiB / 2,344,615,936 bytes (>2GB), mount still shown active, and post-growth checksums still OK.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — an LVM-backed volume mounted at /srv/data, and its live growth to over 2GB with the mount preserved and data integrity verified via before/after checksums — are directly and coherently evidenced. The executor used loopback-file-backed PVs since no spare disk/partition was available on node1, a reasonable and correctly-executed workaround. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also fully and directly evidenced for node1: pre-restart boot identity and healthy baseline, a reboot acknowledgement, connection disruption, a differing post-restart boot identity (cross-checked against the fixed before_prepare/after_executor global boot-identity observations), and full recovery of loop devices, VG/LV, mount, grown filesystem size, and data checksums.
limitations: Growth was demonstrated on loopback-file-backed LVM rather than a physically separate disk, since node1 had no spare block device; this is a reasonable substitution but differs from a typical bare-metal LVM extend scenario.
The single restart cycle observed is a bounded disruption/recovery window; longer-running stability beyond the captured evidence window is not observed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 13 executor commands chronologically. Discovery commands (cmd-bda8662e8f5e4017, cmd-63f9799130174e46) were read-only. State-changing commands (cmd-64827b579d404fa6: LVM/filesystem/mount/service setup; cmd-9174599b11d04620: PV/VG/LV growth) each map directly to a material task outcome. The added persistence unit (lvm-loop-images.service) and fstab entry, while not explicitly required by the public task text, were necessary prerequisites for the loop-backed LVM setup to survive the mandatory reboot used for the independent restart-evidence protocol, and left no orphaned or conflicting state (service ran successfully, no failed units in after_executor snapshot). No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found; failed-services and package-health snapshots are clean before and after. The reboot itself (cmd-9a0264f71cdc43e7) was required for the mandated restart protocol, and its polling/reconnect commands were read-only.
